headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Recovery holds, but short-term traders are hedging

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early uptrend with medium confidence, so this is a sensible time to raise acquisition spend in steps rather than all at once. The 90-day rise and price holding well above its 200-day average support growth budgets, while the still-falling long-term average and a cautious short-term crowd argue for keeping some budget in reserve to add if the recovery firms up. This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a view on where price goes next.

reasons: Price is about 15% above its 200-day average, so the recovery holds.
Up about 33% over 90 days; 60% of those days closed above the long-term average.
The 200-day average still slopes down (-2% over 90 days): an early, unconfirmed recovery.
Mood index 61 (greed), yet bets on a fall with borrowed money are unusually crowded.
watch: The general mood reads greedy, yet an unusually large share of traders are betting on a fall with borrowed money. A close above $86,603 or below $80,936 would show which side was right.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but the coming week looks mixed. Short term, the mood leans slightly cautious: the market mood index reads 61 (greed), yet an unusually large number of traders are betting on a fall with borrowed money. A daily close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, a close below $80,936 (the 50-day average) would turn it down, and in between it likely stays choppy. If those bets on a fall unwind, the mood can flip fast, so keep short promotions flexible rather than locked in.

Over the next month, the picture leans clearly positive: price is up about 33% over 90 days, and 60% of those days closed above the long-term average. News is nudging this down a little, as reports that Iran-linked accounts moved about $850M through Binance add to a US review of the exchange; US inflation data is due next week and the Fed meets on 27 October. While price holds above $80,936 (the 50-day average) the climb stays intact, with room to run above $86,603 (the 90-day high); slipping below that average would fade it. A strong month is when active-trader campaigns usually pay back best.

Over three to six months, the trend leans moderately positive: price is about 15% above its 200-day average, but that average itself is still sloping slightly down (-2% over 90 days). That makes this an early recovery, not a confirmed one. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $71,979 (the 200-day average), with $66,406 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high, 34% away) as the far marker. A 200-day average that starts rising would confirm it and support longer-horizon brand and acquisition plans.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: price is up about 33% over 90 days and most of those days closed above the long-term average, which gives campaigns a real 'recovery' story. With the mood index at 61 but many traders still betting on a fall, lead with education and product depth rather than urgency or fear-of-missing-out. The Ledger reseller theft is a timely hook for security content on how to buy wallets safely and keep recovery words private.

items.why: Starknet's STRK jumped about 42% in a day, with Celestia and Conflux also up more than 20%, though all remain far below their record highs. Earlier October reports tie Starknet's rally to its offer to pay bridge fees for the first 100 BTC moved onto the network; the reports found don't give a clear reason for the latest jump or for the other moves. A scheduled STRK token unlock on 15 October was also reported.
items.marketing_angle: Sharp bounces draw active traders back to smaller tokens, so explainers on what these networks do can catch that interest.

items.why: Ledger confirmed it found an unauthorized hardware implant in a device sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, which has halted all hardware wallet sales; Ledger says its own systems were not compromised. Separately, a fake Ledger website was reported appearing high in Google search results to trick users into revealing their recovery words.
items.marketing_angle: Strong education topic: buy wallets only from official sources, never type recovery words into a website.

items.why: Robinhood said it is exploring stock tokens tied to actively managed ETFs on its own blockchain with T. Rowe Price, while Brazil's main exchange B3 pushed its tokenized-stock platform back to the first half of 2027.
items.marketing_angle: Tokenized stocks remain a strong education and product-awareness topic for users coming from traditional investing.

items.why: Working with T. Rowe Price ($1.9T in assets) on tokenized funds is another step of traditional finance moving onto blockchains, though only at the exploring stage.

summary.short: Confirmation of a tampered Ledger device keeps wallet-safety worries in the headlines for a few more days.
summary.medium: Reports on Binance and Iran-linked accounts add some legal uncertainty for the coming weeks.
summary.long: Robinhood and T. Rowe Price exploring tokenized funds is a small plus for long-run adoption.
